messages:
rachel: Heads-up team: planning a staggered rollout tonight (change window 01:30-03:30 UTC). Services: api v3.2.1, runtime v1.9.1 (batching opt), router v2.4.2, console minor UX patch. I want a short runbook + who takes rollback if things go sideways.
sam: I can own router pinning and immediate fallback. I'll pin router v2.4.2 on the cluster and keep v2.4.0 hot as fallback. Plan: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> drain. 10m observation between steps.
priya: API gating proposal: fail the rollout if api p95 > 700ms or 5xx rate > 0.35% for a 5m window. Manual rollback for API only.
nate: runtime: v1.9.1 enables batching heuristics and a toggle `RUNTIME_QUANT_FALLBACK=true` to disable the new quant path. If we see KV cache misses up 12% or OOMs, revert runtime. I'll be oncall during the window.
rachel: good. Who triggers the rollback command? ops or the owning service?
priya: ops triggers router auto-fallback. For api/runtime we prefer the service lead (me/nate) to call `deploybot rollback` so we can gather logs first, but ops can execute in emergency.
ate: agree. Add an automated anomaly to pause router promotion if router error_rate increases by 0.4% absolute over baseline for 3m.
sam: added. Also keeping a warm hot-fallback route so we can switch without full reconnect storms; will wait 2m after switch to start draining.
deploy-bot: deploybot: scheduled staggered rollout task `wave-003-night` at 01:45 UTC. Canary step: 5% at 01:45, policy: gate via `telemetry.pipeline` events. Use `deploybot promote --wave wave-003-night --step canary`.
priya: release notes ready (short): "wave-003-night: API schema stabilization, runtime batching improvements, router perf fixes, console UX tweak (flagged)." Will circulate to #release-notes and docs.
ate: preflight: runtime smoketest passed in staging; memory delta +1.8%; perf bench stable.
rachel: runbook: 1) start canary 5% 2) check telemetry at +8m and +16m 3) if green -> 25% 4) check +12m -> 75% 5) finalize 100% after 25m stable. If any gate fails, stop and notify #oncall.
sam: small detail: router header changes are backward compatible but we should keep old header parser enabled for 24h in case clients send legacy tokens.
priya: adding client-compat smoke: run 1000 requests against pinned datasets after 25% and check rerank/structure diffs. If rerank drop > 8% vs baseline, hold.\agerbot: pager-bot: alerting schedule loaded: oncall=priya, backup=nate, escalation=sam. Pager channel: #oncall.
priya: also: docs: if we need to rollback, use `deploybot rollback --wave wave-003-night --service <service>` and then create a postmortem draft link in PR template. Lock any feature flags for 48h.
ate: during canary, I'll keep an eye on kvcache churn and schedule a quick heap dump if churn > 10% for debugging.
sam: I'll keep the router pinned and watch connection reset counts. If resets > 0.2% of connections in 5m, signal immediate fallback.
priya: final check: does anyone want auto-fallback for router only? I'm ok with auto-fallback then ops review.
rachel: yes auto-fallback for router only; manual for api/runtime/console. Ops will be allowed to execute manual rollback if the service lead is unreachable.
sam: deploybot: starting canary now -> 5% (timestamp 1718456810). Monitor logs at https://internal.tools/telemetry/wave-003-night.
priya: first telemetry check @ +8m: api p95 420ms, 5xx 0.08%, router errors 0.02%, runtime kv_miss +1.2% 1 good overall.
ate: confirming runtime memory stable. No OOMs.
sam: promoting to 25% now (timestamp 1718456825). Will observe 12m.
rachel: great. Keep this thread as the canonical place for go/no-go notes. If we do a rollback, include the `deploybot` command used and the short reason.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary advanced to 25% at 1718456825.
priya: noted. If all green after 25% hold, we proceed to 75% per runbook. Otherwise, stop and open incident.
priya: thanks everyone 1 we will update with final status in this thread.
